context: Interactive scatter plot of 5000 particles across 8 color-coded categories, using a quadtree for real-time k-nearest-neighbor detection (10 neighbors highlighted on hover), with zoom support and an optional Voronoi overlay.
first_impression: The 8 well-separated clusters read cleanly at a glance despite the particle density, with no visual tangle.
what_works: Spatial cluster separation acts as a second encoding channel beyond color, so the 8-category palette never has to work alone; canvas batching by category keeps 5000 points perceptually manageable with consistent alpha at 0.65. The Tol qualitative palette is perceptually designed and the colors are distinct.
what_doesnt: The grey (#BBBBBB) swatch for Metalloid is the weakest channel — it merges with the background at 65% opacity and is hardest to locate in the legend-to-mark matching task; interaction quality (nearest-neighbor glow, crosshair, Voronoi overlay) cannot be assessed from a static screenshot, which is where the bulk of the cognitive design lives.
